paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, organized by language family, comparing six model configurations: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red/pink), and XLM-B₂ (red). The horizontal axis is labeled "family" and contains nine language family categories arranged from left to right: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is labeled "effect" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately 0 to 30, with tick marks at 0, 10, 20, and 30. Each language family group contains six bars corresponding to the six model configurations, and each bar includes error bars indicating standard deviation. For IE-Baltic, all six bars are relatively small, ranging from roughly 1 to 5. In IE-Germanic, the mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ bars reach approximately 10, the mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ bars are near 0–1, and the mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ bars reach approximately 10 and 15, respectively. The IE-Indic group shows the tallest bars overall, with mBERT-R₂ and XLM-R₂ reaching approximately 18 and 17, mBERT-B₂ reaching approximately 24, and XLM-B₂ approximately 21, while the L₂ variants are notably smaller at roughly 1–2. In IE-Romance, bars range from roughly 0 to 13, with the B₂ variants being the tallest. IE-Slavic shows a similar pattern, with B₂ variants (mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂) reaching approximately 17 and 10, while L₂ and R₂ variants are smaller at roughly 5–9. IE-other displays bars ranging from approximately 5 to 8, with the B₂ variants again being the tallest. The Isolate group shows near-zero effects across all six configurations. The Semitic group has mBERT-L₂ reaching approximately 11–12 and XLM-B₂ reaching approximately 15, but this group displays notably wide error bars extending well above 20 for several configurations, indicating high variability. The Uralic group shows near-zero effects for all configurations, with some bars appearing slightly negative. Error bars vary considerably across families and models, with the Semitic and Uralic families exhibiting particularly large standard deviations relative to bar heights. The bars within each group are not sorted by value but follow a consistent left-to-right ordering matching the legend sequence, and no bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding or outlining beyond the color coding.
